title: Alice & Bob Details QRMI and Slurm 26.11 Hierarchical Resource Integration for Cat-Qubit Systems at SC26 - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Alice & Bob outlined at SC26 in Chicago how its cat-qubit quantum processors integrate with NVIDIA’s open-source Slurm 26.11 workload manager through the vendor-neutral Quantum Resource Management Interface (QRMI). Developed out of a year-long collaboration with the UK’s STFC Hartree Centre alongside open-source contributors from IBM and Pasqal, the architecture connects Alice & Bob’s Felis cloud API directly to standard supercomputing schedulers without requiring per-site custom software.

Whereas earlier Slurm integrations relied on bespoke SPANK plugins to expose quantum hardware, Slurm 26.11 introduces native Hierarchical Resources (HRES) support with Lua plugin bindings that check availability, reserve access, configure compute nodes, and release resources at each stage of a hybrid job. Because Alice & Bob’s cloud backend already implements the QRMI specification, its processors can transition from SPANK-based clusters to the unified QRMI-HRES plugin without additional vendor-side integration work.

Beyond Slurm, the company’s QRMI implementation supports workload scheduling across OpenPBS, IBM Spectrum LSF, Grid Engine, and Flux, as well as an early-stage Kubernetes operator designed to extend quantum resource orchestration into cloud-native clusters. At SC26, engineers from Alice & Bob, IBM, and Pasqal also co-led a technical tutorial demonstrating workload-manager-agnostic QPU execution over QRMI.

Read Alice & Bob’s technical blog post here, review the multi-institutional QRMI technical paper on arXiv here, and explore the open-source QRMI repository on GitHub here.
